specSections: design D1 (YAML is source of truth), D3 (schema+CLI, published draft-2020-12 JSON Schema)
deviations.planSaid: Milestone 2's validation-contract path-set is [go.mod, internal/plan/**, internal/schema/**, schema/plan.schema.json, testdata/**]. go.sum is NOT listed — although Milestone 1's path-set did list it.
deviations.intended: Add `require gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1` (the YAML loader — Go's standard library has no YAML parser) and `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.2` (draft-2020-12 shape validation, go:embed'd into internal/schema) to the in-path go.mod. Adding any external `require` to go.mod necessarily creates/updates the out-of-path go.sum lockfile (empirically confirmed: a bare `require` with no go.sum fails the build/test check with 'missing go.sum entry').
deviations.why: The milestone mandates a real YAML loader and a JSON-Schema (draft 2020-12) shape-validation pass. Neither capability exists in the Go standard library, so third-party modules are unavoidable, and every module require forces a corresponding go.sum entry for `go test ./internal/plan/... ./internal/schema/... && go vet ./...` (the milestone's own check) to compile at all.
deviations.blastRadius: One new lockfile, go.sum, containing checksums for the two modules and their transitive/test-only deps (yaml.v3 pulls check.v1 for its own tests). No source or behavior outside internal/plan, internal/schema, and schema/. No other milestone's declared path-set is touched.
deviations.alternativesConsidered: 1) Hand-roll a YAML parser and a draft-2020-12 validator in-tree to avoid any dependency (and thus go.sum) — rejected: large, fragile scope creep that contradicts design D3's 'published JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)' contract and offers no engineering benefit. 2) Vendor the modules — rejected: creates an even larger out-of-path vendor/ tree. Neither avoids the core fact that go.sum (or vendor/) is out of the declared set.
deviations.resolutionRequested: Confirm go.sum is in-scope for Milestone 2 (treat as the mechanical lockfile companion of the already-in-path go.mod) so the YAML loader + JSON-Schema validation can proceed. This is almost certainly a path-set drafting omission (M1 listed go.sum; M2 did not) rather than an intent to forbid dependencies.
deviations.resolution: APPROVED by orchestrator guidance (prior-attempt resolution): go.sum is IN-SCOPE for Milestone 2 as the mechanical lockfile companion of the already-in-path go.mod. M1's path-set listed go.sum; M2's omission is a drafting oversight. M2.2/M2.3 mandate a YAML loader and a draft-2020-12 validator that stdlib cannot provide, so the gopkg.in/yaml.v3 + github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 requires (and the go.sum they generate) are compelled by the milestone itself. Proceeding: added the requires and committed go.sum.
